source.manufacturer: Texas Instruments (TI Tech Days presentation, Tomas Urban, Systems Engineering - Automotive Powertrain Systems)
source.document_id: SLYP685, 'Be confident around automotive functional safety' - worked FMEDA example slides 'Example n=1' .. 'Example n=4' and slide 'Example of FS FIT rates acc. to SN29500'

note: H-09 (issue #56) tool-qualification fixture for tools/fmeda-calculator.py (ISO 26262-8 section 13, TCL2 regression; OR-004). The four iterations of the public TI example are fully specified (FIT, failure-mode distribution, safety-goal violation, safety mechanism, diagnostic coverage) and every FIT-level result is reproduced exactly by the calculator. Publication precision disposition: the slide percentages are printed to one decimal; the calculator reproduces 49.5 %, 90.9 % and 50.0 % exactly; for n=3 the slide prints 'LFM = 1-(10/(121-11)) = 90.1 %' although the printed fraction evaluates to 90.9 % (a transcription slip in the source), and for n=4 the slide prints 98.8 % and 84.5 % where half-up rounding of the printed fractions gives 98.9 % and 84.6 % (the source truncated). The regression asserts the printed fractions and FIT sums exactly and the percentages under the documented disposition; it never adjusts the arithmetic to match a typo. The PMHF values on the slides use the source's own simplification PMHF = sum(RF) + sum(MPF,latent), which the calculator reports as 'pmhf_source_simplified_fit' next to the ISO 26262-5 Annex C / ISO 26262-10 forms. Also transcribed: the SN 29500 class values TI tabulates (secondary tabulation) used by hw/bom/fit-database.json. No PDF is retained; source_url is TI's own hosting of the document.
